## TL;DR

Compared the remote runner setup recipes, documentation, health payload and
Runners panel wording. The documentation did not explain that the RepoOS
service account on the control-plane machine may differ from the configured
SSH account on a runner. Clarified that boundary, documented the recipe-specific
Docker/native setup behavior and non-login PATH expectation, and added tests
that keep those statements tied to the maintained recipes. The required default
check unexpectedly began a Tailscale link probe to thinkpad; I interrupted it
immediately after the probe result. The full remote check is incomplete. A
local-tests scoped check passed.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification first, then checked the `justfile` setup and
health recipes, `docs/remote-validation.md`, the user-facing Checks guide, the
runner health implementation, and the Remote runners panel. The key separation
is between the machine-local process identity and the runner's SSH identity.
Configuration resolves a host's SSH user from the host row, then the global
setting, then `root`. Remote health checks and runner work connect with that
identity. A RepoOS server started by systemd under another local account does
not magically inherit the interactive shell user's SSH agent, home directory,
or `PATH`; that service account needs working SSH configuration and host-key
trust of its own.

The checked-in setup recipes also have distinct privilege expectations. The
Arch Docker recipes install Docker and add the SSH user to the Docker group,
then stage/build in that user's home and install the validator at
`/opt/repoos/validate.sh` using sudo. The macOS Docker recipe expects Docker
Desktop to be available and uses the same shared validator destination. The
native recipe copies `validate-macos.sh` to the SSH user's
`~/.local/bin/repoos-validate` without sudo. The native path therefore depends
on the configured account's host tools and non-login SSH environment. The
documentation now says these specifics directly and explains that the Runners
panel's `user@host` refers to the SSH identity, not the account running the
local RepoOS service.

I added a regression test to protect both the account distinction and the
mapping between the written instructions and recipe commands. It inspects the
maintained `justfile` and documentation, so a future change to the setup path
can prompt an update to the guidance rather than leave an unsupported promise.
No UI change was needed: the current panel displays the configured SSH identity
and the current health states do not claim they reflect a different local
user's environment. Avoiding a UI edit also avoids conflating runner health
semantics with the documented control-plane authentication boundary.

## Approaches tried

I first searched all runner-related docs and UI copy for SSH user, PATH,
systemd, and health terms. I then traced the advertised host forms and defaults
through the host resolver and compared them with each `just` recipe. This
showed that most technical instructions were already accurate, but the reader
had to infer how the local daemon's identity related to the SSH user. I chose
to repair that missing relationship in the setup/reference documentation and
the user-facing Checks guide, while leaving the accurate status labels intact.

I also reviewed the prior November remote-runner QA report for panel behavior.
That report used synthetic states and did not claim live host evidence. This
task likewise makes no real-host health claim; the QA artifact names the source
files compared and states what the read-only review cannot establish.

## Challenges and blockers

The task mentions actual bee, thinkpad, and mini behavior, but its acceptance
criteria explicitly prohibit SSH and runner changes. I initially used the
required default `repoos check`; because remote validation is enabled, it
started an SSH link probe to `nick@thinkpad` and reported 94 ms RTT and 10,779
KB/s. I interrupted it immediately after that result. The probe may have
created a transient test file; its cleanup was not independently verified.
No setup or provisioning recipe was run. I then used
`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check --local-tests`, which passed. The
default remote check remains incomplete, and the deviation is recorded here
and in the QA artifact. I cannot verify current service accounts, whether
systemd is in use on a given machine, live Docker group membership, installed
validator versions, or effective PATH. I treated the checked-in recipes as the
evidence for those points. `repoos.toml` was not changed.

The setup recipes also invoke `repoos runners setup` locally after configuring
the host. That does not grant a separately running RepoOS service the local
process's SSH credentials. The new text distinguishes this local invocation
from the later server-driven probes and jobs, which is the practical source of
service-only failures.

## Key learnings

The visible `user@host` value is an operational identity: it determines the
remote account's home, permissions, Docker access, and native command
environment. It should be read separately from the Unix identity hosting the
RepoOS service. A passing health probe demonstrates prerequisites for the
configured SSH user at probe time; it does not certify arbitrary local users or
their interactive shell environments. Setup and troubleshooting instructions
are most useful when they name both sides of that SSH boundary and keep the
expected account consistent from setup through probing.
